analysis.evidence: וְהָיָה introduces the situation Abram foresees. כִּי יִרְאוּ אֹתָךְ הַמִּצְרִים sets the time, “when the Egyptians see you,” and וְאָמְרוּ introduces what they will say.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ precedes the Qal perfect third-person masculine singular. The resulting weqatal has future reference in Abram’s prediction.

analysis.evidence: After וְהָיָה, כִּי introduces the anticipated event “when the Egyptians see you.” The following וְאָמְרוּ introduces what they will then say.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew conjunction with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In כִּי יִרְאוּ אֹתָךְ הַמִּצְרִים, “when the Egyptians see you,” אֹתָךְ marks Sarai as the direct object. The Egyptians see her and then say, “This is his wife.”
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, third person masculine plural, agreeing with הַמִּצְרִים in the anticipated event.

analysis.evidence: הַמִּצְרִים is the plural subject of יִרְאוּ אֹתָךְ, “they will see you.” Abram expects these Egyptians to say that Sarai is his wife, kill him, and let her live.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ precedes a masculine plural gentilic in the absolute state. The gentilic adjective functions as a noun.

analysis.evidence: Abram predicts what the Egyptians (הַמִּצְרִים) will say when they see Sarai. Their words follow immediately in אִשְׁתּוֹ זֹאת, “This is his wife.”
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ prefixes a Qal perfect, third person common plural. In this predictive sequence, the verb has future force.

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 68619:8, 68613:4, 66585:4, 66577:3, 66561:4, 66324:3.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular construct noun with the third-person masculine singular possessive suffix ־וֹ.

analysis.evidence: The Egyptians are the subject, and אֹתִי (“me”) identifies Abram as the person they will kill. He contrasts his expected fate with Sarai’s in וְאֹתָךְ יְחַיּוּ (“and they will keep you alive”).
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ precedes the Qal perfect third common plural הָרְגוּ. In this predictive sequence, the verb expresses what the Egyptians will do.

analysis.evidence: Abram contrasts וְהָרְגוּ אֹתִי, “they will kill me,” with וְאֹתָךְ יְחַיּוּ, “but you they will let live.” The fronted object אֹתָךְ identifies Sarai as the one the Egyptians will spare.
analysis.morphology: Piel imperfect, third person masculine plural. The subject is the Egyptians.
